raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`SRTPlatform.get_paged_allocator_cls()` lets a platform replace the paged KV allocator, and its docstring says it is "honored at every paged-allocator construction site". At `page_size == 1`, though, two sites construct `TokenToKVPoolAllocator` directly and never consult the platform:

- the KV cache configurator (`kv_cache_configurator.py`, the `page_size == 1 and not dcp_enabled` branch);
- `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.__init__`, in its `page_size == 1` branch.

A platform that needs a different allocator has to monkeypatch the module-level name at page size 1. Examples: CPU-resident free-list bookkeeping, or no device `free_pages` kernels.

## Modifications

- New `SRTPlatform.get_token_allocator_cls() -> Optional[type]`, default `None`. `None` keeps `TokenToKVPoolAllocator`. The class is constructed with the same arguments as the in-tree one.
- Both page-size-1 sites use `current_platform.get_token_allocator_cls() or TokenToKVPoolAllocator`.

Nothing changes for in-tree platforms (they all return `None`).

## How it was found

Found while building an out-of-tree Neuron/Trainium platform plugin. Qwen3.5 serves at `page_size == 1`, where upstream builds `TokenToKVPoolAllocator`, whose device `free_pages` cannot take the CPU indices the plugin's host paths free. The plugin currently patches `kv_cache_configurator.TokenToKVPoolAllocator` to return its paged allocator at one token per page.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. There is no behavior change for in-tree platforms.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Tests

- Run (macOS, CPU only): `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_platform_token_allocator_hook.py` (new). It checks that the hook defaults to `None`, that `SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` at page size 1 builds the platform class for both sub-allocators, and that it defaults to `TokenToKVPoolAllocator`. Also ran `test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py`. 77 passed in total.
- Not run: the configurator branch is not unit-tested; it is a one-line change. No GPU run.

## Open questions

- Alternatively, `get_paged_allocator_cls()` could be honored at page size 1 too (constructing it with `page_size=1`). That is what the plugin does internally. It would change behavior for platforms that already override the paged class (NPU, XPU, ...), so I kept a separate hook. Happy to fold them together if preferred.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""CPU tests for ``SRTPlatform.get_token_allocator_cls`` (page_size == 1)."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator import swa as swa_allocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.token import TokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_swa_memory_pool import BaseSWAKVPool
+from sglang.srt.platforms.interface import SRTPlatform
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+class _RecordingAllocator(TokenToKVPoolAllocator):
+    built = []
+
+    def __init__(self, size, dtype, device, kvcache, need_sort):
+        type(self).built.append(size)
+        super().__init__(size, dtype, device, kvcache, need_sort)
+
+
+def _platform(token_cls):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        get_token_allocator_cls=lambda: token_cls,
+        get_paged_allocator_cls=lambda: None,
+    )
+
+
+def _build_swa():
+    kvcache = MagicMock(spec=BaseSWAKVPool)
+    kvcache.full_kv_pool = MagicMock()
+    kvcache.swa_kv_pool = MagicMock()
+    kvcache.swa_req_ring_size = None
+    return swa_allocator.SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+        size=16,
+        size_swa=8,
+        page_size=1,
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+        device="cpu",
+        kvcache=kvcache,
+        need_sort=False,
+    )
+
+
+class TestPlatformTokenAllocatorHook(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_default_is_none(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(SRTPlatform.get_token_allocator_cls(MagicMock()))
+
+    def test_swa_page1_uses_platform_class(self):
+        _RecordingAllocator.built = []
+        with patch.object(
+            swa_allocator, "current_platform", _platform(_RecordingAllocator)
+        ):
+            alloc = _build_swa()
+        self.assertIsInstance(alloc.full_attn_allocator, _RecordingAllocator)
+        self.assertIsInstance(alloc.swa_attn_allocator, _RecordingAllocator)
+        self.assertEqual(_RecordingAllocator.built, [16, 8])
+
+    def test_swa_page1_defaults_to_in_tree_class(self):
+        with patch.object(swa_allocator, "current_platform", _platform(None)):
+            alloc = _build_swa()
+        self.assertIs(type(alloc.full_attn_allocator), TokenToKVPoolAllocator)
+        self.assertIs(type(alloc.swa_attn_allocator), TokenToKVPoolAllocator)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
